Dear Chris, 
Subject: April 1, 2018 to March 31, 2019 ASC 712 Expense Results—KeySpan 
Enclosed is the fiscal year 2019 ASC 712 expense valuation for KeySpan. The valuation is based on 
January 1, 2018 data provided by National Grid. Based on a 3.65 percent discount rate assumption, 
the incremental operating expense for the period April 1, 2018 through March 31, 2019 is $1.7 
million. 
Fiscal Year 2019 Valuation Results 
The plan’s overall experience in fiscal year 2019 was less favorable than budgeted. In aggregate, the 
projected liability at year-end was $3.2 million higher than expected. 
The key items that impacted the liability included: 
▪
Unfavorable claims experience for union plans
▪
A change in medical trend rates; and
▪
An increase in LTD claimants; offset by
▪
A change in discount rate from 3.30% to 3.65%; and
▪
Favorable claims experience for non-union plans
Enclosed is a summary of expense/(income) by business unit, as well as a summary of the 
assumptions and benefit provisions used in the valuation. 
Preparation of this Actuarial Valuation 
This valuation has been prepared to present to management the necessary information to comply 
with ASC 712-10 for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2019. Determinations for purposes other than 
financial accounting requirements may be significantly different from the results reported herein. 
Thus, the use of this information for purposes other than those expressed here may not be 
appropriate. The results as of other dates may also be significantly different from the results reported 
herein.

In conducting the valuation, we have relied on personnel, plan design and health care claim cost 
supplied by National Grid. While we cannot verify the accuracy of all of the supplied information, the 
information was reviewed for consistency and reasonability. As a result of this review, we have no 
reason to doubt the substantial accuracy or completeness of the information and believe that it has 
produced appropriate results. 
This valuation has been conducted in accordance with generally accepted actuarial principles and 
practices, including the applicable Actuarial Standards of Practice as issued by the Actuarial 
Standards Board. In addition, the valuation results are based on our understanding of the 
requirements of ASC 712-10. The information in this report is not intended to supersede or supplant 
the advice and interpretations of National Grid’s auditors. 
The actuarial assumptions and methods used in this valuation are described in the ASC 712 
Assumptions and Methods section. National Grid selected the economic, demographic, and health 
care claims cost assumptions and prescribed them for use for purposes of compliance with ASC 712-
10. Aon provided guidance with respect to these assumptions, and it is our belief that they represent 
reasonable expectations of anticipated plan experience. The actuarial cost method is prescribed by 
ASC 712-10.

Dear Chris, 
Subject: April 1, 2018 to March 31, 2019 ASC 712 Expense Results—New England 
Enclosed is the fiscal year 2019 ASC 712 expense valuation for New England. The valuation is based 
on January 1, 2018 data provided by National Grid. Based on a 3.65 percent discount rate 
assumption, the incremental operating expense for the period April 1, 2018 through March 31, 2019 
is $1.4 million. 
Fiscal Year 2019 Valuation Results 
The plan’s overall experience in fiscal year 2019 was more favorable than budgeted. In aggregate, 
the projected liability at year-end was $0.3 million lower than expected. 
The key items that impacted the liability included: 
▪ 
Fewer participants with life insurance and income replacement benefits 
▪ 
A change in discount rate from 3.30% to 3.65%; and 
▪ 
Lower medical costs; offset by 
▪ 
Increased future medical trend rates  
▪ 
Larger active population; and 
▪ 
Small increase in claimants with medical benefits;  
Enclosed is a summary of expense/(income) by company, as well as a summary of the assumptions 
and benefit provisions used in the valuation. 
Preparation of this Actuarial Valuation 
This valuation has been prepared to present to management the necessary information to comply 
with ASC 712-10 for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2019. Determinations for purposes other than 
financial accounting requirements may be significantly different from the results reported herein. 
Thus, the use of this information for purposes other than those expressed here may not be 
appropriate. The results as of other dates may also be significantly different from the results reported 
herein.

In conducting the valuation, we have relied on personnel, plan design and health care claim cost 
supplied by National Grid. While we cannot verify the accuracy of all of the supplied information, the 
information was reviewed for consistency and reasonability. As a result of this review, we have no 
reason to doubt the substantial accuracy or completeness of the information and believe that it has 
produced appropriate results. 
This valuation has been conducted in accordance with generally accepted actuarial principles and 
practices, including the applicable Actuarial Standards of Practice as issued by the Actuarial 
Standards Board. In addition, the valuation results are based on our understanding of the 
requirements of ASC 712-10. The information in this report is not intended to supersede or supplant 
the advice and interpretations of National Grid’s auditors. 
The actuarial assumptions and methods used in this valuation are described in the ASC 712 
Assumptions and Methods section. National Grid selected the economic, demographic, and health 
care claims cost assumptions and prescribed them for use for purposes of compliance with ASC 
712-10. Aon provided guidance with respect to these assumptions, and it is our belief that they 
represent reasonable expectations of anticipated plan experience. The actuarial cost method is 
prescribed by ASC 712-10.

Dear Chris, 
Subject: April 1, 2018 to March 31, 2019 ASC 712 Expense Results—Niagara Mohawk 
Enclosed is the fiscal year 2019 ASC 712 expense valuation for Niagara Mohawk. The valuation is 
based on January 1, 2018 data provided by National Grid. Based on a 3.65 percent discount rate 
assumption, the incremental operating income for the period April 1, 2018 through March 31, 2019 is 
$1.8 million. 
Fiscal Year 2019 Valuation Results 
The plan’s overall experience in fiscal year 2019 was more favorable than budgeted. In aggregate, 
the projected liability at year-end was $0.8 million lower than expected, mainly due to a higher 
discount rate. 
The key items that impacted the liability included: 
▪ 
A change in discount rate from 3.30% to 3.65%  
▪ 
Slightly smaller active population; and 
▪ 
Decrease in union income replacement claimants; offset by 
▪ 
Higher expected medical costs for both union and non-union employees; and 
▪ 
Increased future medical trend rates  
Enclosed is a summary of expense/(income), as well as a summary of the assumptions and benefit 
provisions used in the valuation.

Preparation of this Actuarial Valuation 
This valuation has been prepared to present to management the necessary information to comply 
with ASC 712-10 for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2019. Determinations for purposes other than 
financial accounting requirements may be significantly different from the results reported herein. 
Thus, the use of this information for purposes other than those expressed here may not be 
appropriate. The results as of other dates may also be significantly different from the results reported 
herein. 
In conducting the valuation, we have relied on personnel, plan design and health care claim cost 
supplied by National Grid. While we cannot verify the accuracy of all of the supplied information, the 
information was reviewed for consistency and reasonability. As a result of this review, we have no 
reason to doubt the substantial accuracy or completeness of the information and believe that it has 
produced appropriate results. 
This valuation has been conducted in accordance with generally accepted actuarial principles and 
practices, including the applicable Actuarial Standards of Practice as issued by the Actuarial 
Standards Board. In addition, the valuation results are based on our understanding of the 
requirements of ASC 712-10. The information in this report is not intended to supersede or supplant 
the advice and interpretations of National Grid’s auditors.

INITIATIVE DESCRIPTION
During FY18, a competitive bid event was executed resulting in a Time & Material contract with Tri-Messine to be a secondary paving contractor in NYC to pick up additional work the existing contractor cannot perform.  The T&M contract was effective from Sept 2017 
through July 2018. Tri-Messine started work in Oct 2017.  
In August 2018, an extension to Tri-Messine’s contract was negotiated resulting in a new expiration date of March 31, 2019 and a conversion to a Unit Price contract, and reducing National Grid’s secondary paving contractor costs.
The current contract will expire on 3/31/19 and the initiative being executed now is a negotiation of a 2 year extension to their contract.
Using the spend for the work assigned in FY18 (~ 6 months) as the baseline, we estimated a 10% benefits as a result of converting the T&M pricing into Unit Pricing for FY19. Consequently, the second negotiation further reduced the unit price (~6%) and will result in 
additional benefits in FY20 and FY21. As a result, we are estimating a total of 16% benefits against FY18 spend.
US Construction - Tri-Messine Contract Extension Negotiation
